text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `az2-serving-pool-queue-surge` (severity: high) — multiple downstream timeouts. Routing: az2.
PagerDuty: Incident created and notified oncall. Count=4 alerts grouped by: queue_depth>1000, kv_cache_miss_spike, grpc_timeouts.
Samir (oncall): acked. I'm jumping in now, assigning myself. @Rupa you on rotation for handoff?
Rupa: I'm available for handoff in 5. if you need escalation ping me.
Samir (oncall): quick triage: dashboards show az2 serving pool queue_depth ~ 2.3k, p95 token-latency from az2 up to 280ms. Other regions ok.
Maya: seeing an uptick in 502/504 from embeddings endpoint for some customers. Not full outage but large error increase. customer-impact=partial-degradation.
Samir (oncall): running quick health commands:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=az2-serving -o wide
rctl pool-stats az2-serving --window=5m
```
Samir (oncall): logs show repeated `worker pool busy` and `eviction-delay` messages. KV cache misses jumped after a deployment 10m ago.
Kai: FYI the routing policy has auto-failover enabled for az2 -> will start redirecting new requests to az1/az3 when latency breach sustained >3m. That kicked in ~1m ago.
incident-bot: Auto-failover activated for region=az2. Route fallback: weight(az2:60% -> az1:20%, az3:20%) then ramp.
Jesse: Can we increase az2 capacity while fallback ramps? I can request +2 GPU nodes to dedicated pool, but it takes ~4-6m to spin. Acceptable?
Samir (oncall): Yes please. Jesse go ahead. Also I'm going to temporarily disable a recent model variant rollout that increased memory pressure.
Jesse: doing node add: `infracli resize --pool az2-serving --add-gpu 2 --reason "surge"` — submitted. provisioning started.
Rupa: Confirming customer routes—critical customers (enterprise) already moved to reserved capacity in az1. The impacted set is mostly free/standard workloads -> temporary latency increase only. No customer data loss reported.
Maya: I see error rates dropping slowly as fallback weights mature. p50 latency still up but p95 trending down.
Samir (oncall): doing KV cache priming on az1/az3 to reduce miss amplification. Running priming job: `priming-job --targets az1,az3 --models embed/v2`
Samir (oncall): Also rolling back the last canary deploy on az2: `deployctl rollback canary embed/v2-canary`
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: acknowledgement recorded by Samir (oncall). Escalation threshold (10m) not yet reached.
Jesse: new nodes reporting ready in az2. capacity +2 GPUs applied, autoscaler overridden to hold for 15m.
Kai: routing weights now: az2 85% (after capacity), az1 8%, az3 7% — auto-failover reversed partially per policy because primary latency improved.
Maya: customer-facing metrics: error-rate back to baseline for 87% of customers. A small percentage still seeing intermittent retries. Logging shows retry storms from clients with tight timeouts.
Samir (oncall): marking incident as mitigation in place. Will keep watch for 20m, then unpage if stable. Please add any customer reports here.
Rupa: I'll open a follow-up postmortem ticket with timeline, root-cause hypothesis (cache miss spike + recent canary memory regression) and action items (improve priming, tighter deployment guardrails).
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident resolved (mitigated) by Samir (oncall). Auto-failover returned to normal.
Samir (oncall): closing thread for now. Follow-up: postmortem + deploy guardrails. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
